title: Two HD 93683 fits give a companion mass floor near 0.25 solar masses without an inner eccentricity cap between epochs
abstract: We test whether unobserved inner eccentricity growth can remove a companion mass floor from HD 93683 eclipse fits. We bound the full angular momentum vector torque, rather than the unit-normal speed. Conservation puts its path on a sphere set by the outer angular momentum. The shortest arc and an endpoint-based bound on inner angular momentum give a necessary mass test without a global inner eccentricity cap. For two published point fits, inner masses of 18 and 15 solar masses, and endpoint eccentricities at most their fitted values, the mass floors are 0.2508 and 0.2543 solar masses. Outer period, eccentricity, nodes and photometric inclination branches are free within double-averaged quadrupole dynamics. A simpler analytic bound gives 0.2234 and 0.2267 solar masses. We provide a proof, explicit numerical brackets, sensitivity tests, 200,000 random torque checks and twelve synthetic secular integrations with outer response. These are conditional necessary bounds, not detections or confidence limits. The result needs endpoint constraints and the averaged model; it does not apply to all Newtonian triples, changing outer angular momentum magnitude or extra torque sources.
